items.title: Driver arrested for allegedly ramming rideshare vehicle, road closed after hills crash

children.content: A 19-year-old driver who allegedly rammed a rideshare vehicle has been arrested. Meanwhile after a separate incident, road closures are in place after a fatal crash at Paracombe, north-east of Adelaide.

items.title: Farmer fined $60k for clearing native vegetation north of Adelaide

children.content: A 73-year-old farmer is fined $60,000 for clearing more than 250 hectares of native vegetation at a property at Port Wakefield.

image.altText: A green low-lying samphire plant

items.title: Short-stay operators have mixed reactions to SA's register proposal

children.content: The scheme is still being shaped but some operators are raising concerns about security and giving local governments control over land use and deciding rates.

image.altText: A man with hat stands in front on a modern short term rental property in a regional area.

items.title: SA's first musical theatre company brings talent home in debut stage

children.content: Performers like Joey Haenen and Jazz Garcia who sought opportunities on the east coast are returning to Adelaide in Full Circle's debut production of SA's first musical theatre company.

items.title: SA government says prior parklands works set precedent for MotoGP circuit

children.content: The city O-Bahn tunnel and new Women's and Children's Hospital have set precedents for major work in the Adelaide parklands, the state government has argued in a MotoGP circuit assessment.

image.altText: a drone shot of Victoria Park with an Adelaide sign on the road

items.title: Regional audiences to lose Network 10, as licensee warns of TV's future

children.content: After a three-month reprieve, WIN confirms Network 10 will go from Mount Gambier, the Riverland and Griffith.

image.altText: Sign of the number 10 in a blue circle on a brown wall

items.title: Harvest starts on SA crops that 'have not had a setback all season'

children.content: South Australia's crops, sown early on the back of good autumn rain, are ready for harvest. Logistically, it is going to be a big, difficult harvest but "what a great problem" to have, says a grower.

image.altText: Light green heads of wheat up in a paddock.

items.title: Could exposure to sharks reduce fear and boost conservation efforts?

children.content: Watching Jaws as a child led to Juliana Gleave's fascination with sharks. Now, with their numbers reduced by 70 per cent since the movie was released, she is working to see if familiarity can lead to better conservation awareness.

image.altText: Cage-diving with a big shark

items.title: Diseases of the past like measles and diphtheria are making a comeback

children.content: A recent outbreak of measles in Adelaide has sparked concern from health authorities, but it's not the only infectious illness where cases are rising once again.

image.altText: A young girl receives a vaccination from a man in a white coat in an undated black and white photograph.

items.title: Nobel Peace Prize won't go to Trump this year, experts say

children.content: It is often regarded as the most prestigious of all Nobel prizes, which are given to those who have "conferred the greatest benefit to humankind". But the Nobel Peace Prize can also be controversial.

image.altText: Donald Trump is nominated for the prize but experts think it is unlikely he will win.

items.title: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announces early election

children.content: Spain's prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has called an early election as the country grapples with a housing crisis.

image.altText: A middle-aged man gestures as he speaks in front of a number of flags in a gilded room.

items.title: US accuses California woman of spying on Taiwan president's son for China

children.content: The FBI says authorities have arrested a California woman and accused her of spying on a son of Taiwan's president at the direction of Chinese officials.

image.altText: A woman is being led in handcuffs along a corridor, surrounded by three agents wearing jackets with FBI written on the back.

items.title: NBL owner pays Tasmanian government $577 a week to rent stadium

children.content: The Tasmanian government has effectively been leasing out a stadium to property developer and NBL owner Larry Kestelman for less than it would cost to rent most houses in the area, a parliamentary report has found.

items.title: WA premier backflips on desalination plant amid $543m pipeline upgrade

children.content: The WA government is weighing up future plans for a desalination plant in Esperance as work on a $543 million upgrade to the historic Goldfields water pipeline ramps up.

image.altText: A water pipeline in the outback at sunset.

items.title: Former Bachelor star Sam Wood will stay behind bars after facing court on DV charges

children.content: Fitness influencer and former Bachelor contestant Sam Wood will remain behind bars after facing court for several domestic violence charges following his arrest in Noosa on the weekend.

children.content: An independent review by the Professional Standards Command will be conducted after a man was fatally shot by NSW police near Yass on Sunday.

children.content: Alongside five mates, Hayden Sumner has completed a cross-country relay from Perth to Sydney in honour of his late mother, who spent years in abusive relationships.

items.title: More than 5,000 pepper spray canisters sold in the NT since start of trial

children.content: A report on the sale and use of pepper spray for self-defence in the Northern Territory under a government trial has found 3,714 people have bought the product so far, with 46 prohibited buyers identified and three non-lawful deployments recorded.

items.title: Illegal tobacco crackdown in Victoria has come too late, says ex-policeman

children.content: Premier Ben Carroll has conceded the Victorian government should have acted sooner on illegal tobacco but insisted progress had been made since the new enforcement powers came into effect.

items.title: Samoan PM apologises for 'heil Hitler' salute at family event in 2007

children.content: Laaulialemalietoa Leuatea Schmidt apologises after video emerges of him performing a Nazi salute and saying the phrase "heil Hitler" at a family event in 2007.

image.altText: La'aulialemalietoa Leuatea Schmidt wearing a brightly coloured shirt.

items.title: Flydubai co-pilot planned to crash plane into airport, Israeli media reports

children.content: The flydubai co-pilot allegedly tells investigators he intended to continue flying normally before crashing into the main airport in Israel.

items.title: Ketamine cold calls and 'free' cannabis: Veterans treated as 'cash cows'

children.content: For nearly two years, veteran Steve Johnstone was prescribed huge quantities of high-THC cannabis by doctors he had never spoken to.
